Lokachi Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Lokachi holds a place of profound significance in Hasidic history: Dov Baer, known as the Maggid of Mezritch — the disciple and successor of the Baal Shem Tov who was chiefly responsible for spreading Hasidism throughout Eastern Europe after the Besht's death, and whose grave is documented at Hannopil elsewhere in this collection — was born in Lokachi in 1704. Jews are first mentioned in the town in 1569, reaching 907 by 1765 and supporting Olyka, Trisk, and Ruzhin Hasidic streams across five synagogues by 1885; the population reached 1,730 (75 percent) by 1897. A vibrant interwar cultural life included a library established by I.L. Peretz, Zionist youth organizations, and a Tarbut school. Following the June 1941 occupation, a ghetto's September 1942 liquidation saw 1,350 Jews shot; a monument was installed at the execution site in 1989. This cemetery, presumably dating to the 16th or 17th century, was most likely demolished after WWII, with final destruction in the 1980s-90s, when a fire station and private houses were built on the site.
